questions.topic: PrepLadder · 28.Renal Tubular Acidosis and Renal Artery Stenosis
questions.stem: A 42-year-old woman comes to the OPD due to the passage of blood in her urine, along with complaints of left flank pain, fatigue and generalised weakness. She has a history of recurrent renal stones. USG confirmed the presence of renal stones in her left renal pelvis. Lab reports show the following values. Based on the values given below, what is the most likely diagnosis? Blood pH - 7.29 Serum sodium - 144 mEq/L Serum potassium - 3.1 mEq/L Serum bicarbonate - 9 mEq/L Urine pH - 5.8 Urine calcium - elevated Urine citrate - low Normal anion gap
